mainTopic: Who is believed about a בכור's or a מעשר animal's blemish, and when three ordinary people may permit a בכור
overview: This amud finishes a discussion from the previous amud about רב's rule that a כהן is believed when he says a ישראל gave him a בכור already blemished, because people do not lie about something that can be checked. A proof from a משנה about an agent buying produce is offered and then rejected. רבי ירמיה בר אבא then says the teaching was changed as it was passed down, and that in the original version it is the ישראל who is believed. The הלכה follows even the first version, so even a כהן is believed. A story about רפרם, who caught a lying כהן, shows that one brazen person does not make all כהנים suspect. רב אשי then rules that a בכור born with an obvious blemish raises no concern, even when a ישראל brings it without a כהן present. Next, a משנה teaches that everyone is believed about blemishes on a מעשר animal, because the owner could have blemished his whole flock before tithing. A further משנה lets three ordinary people permit a בכור with an obvious blemish, while רבי יוסי requires a מומחה. The גמרא limits this leniency to clear-cut blemishes and to places with no expert, and it begins explaining a parallel rule about annulling vows that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The agent can easily wriggle out of blame
steps.stepSummary: The end of an answer: in the first clause of the משנה the agent is not believed, because he has an easy excuse.
steps.simpleTranslation: …because he has a way to wriggle out of it.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last line of the גמרא's answer about the first clause of the משנה, where the agent is not believed. The גמרא says that case is different because the agent can easily excuse himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first clause, the agent was only told to buy from 'a reliable person,' with no name given. If he lied, he could just say, 'I thought the seller was reliable.' Since he has an easy way out, he is not afraid to lie, so he is not believed. That case therefore does not contradict רב's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: to slip away / wriggle out of blame by making an excuse
since he has

steps.confusionAlert: This line is the end of an answer that started on the previous amud. It is not a new statement on its own.

phrases.english: since he has a way to slip out of it.
phrases.notes: He can say, 'I thought the seller was reliable.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the answer earlier about the first clause of the משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case: the person has an easy excuse
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The agent who is not believed in the first clause seems to go against רב's rule that people don't lie about checkable facts.
steps.terutzMaskana: There, the agent can claim he honestly thought the seller was reliable, so he has no fear of being caught. This does not contradict רב.

steps.title: The second clause of the משנה seems to support רב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the סיפא of the משנה clearly supports רב: when the agent was told to buy from a specific named person, he is believed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The last clause surely supports him: if he was told 'from so-and-so,' the agent is believed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now offers a proof for רב from the second half of the same משנה. Here the agent was sent to buy from one named person, and he is believed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a specific seller was named, anyone can go ask that seller what happened. So the agent would not lie about something that can easily be checked. This looks exactly like רב's reason: people don't lie about what can come to light.

keyTerms.meaning: the last clause of a משנה or ברייתא
it certainly supports him
a certain person, so-and-so (someone named)
believed, trusted

phrases.english: The last clause certainly supports him (רב):
'(Buy) from so-and-so': this agent is believed.
phrases.notes: Because the named seller can be asked.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After explaining away the first clause, the גמרא turns to the second clause as positive support.
steps.raayaObject: רב's rule that a person is believed about a fact that can be checked, such as the כהן's claim about the blemished בכור
steps.raayaSupportSource: The סיפא of the משנה about an agent buying produce from a named person

steps.title: The proof is rejected: there, someone is clearly going to check
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. In the משנה, the agent knows a specific claimant may check up on him, so he is afraid to lie. That is not the same as רב's case.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, since he has someone who will check up on him, he is afraid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof from the סיפא. The משנה's case is stronger than רב's case, so it proves nothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, the person who sent the agent named the seller himself. The agent assumes his boss plans to check, so he is scared to lie. In רב's case, the כהן is the one who brought up the ישראל's name, and nobody plans to check. So the כהן may not be afraid at all.

keyTerms.meaning: there (in that other case)
a claimant: someone who will demand an accounting
he is afraid / trembles

phrases.english: There, since he has a claimant (who may check),
he is afraid (to lie).

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם, כֵּיוָן דְּאִית לֵיהּ תּוֹבֵעַ, מִירְתַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in Step 2.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof is rejected. רב's rule itself is not disproven.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה has a sender who named the seller and will likely check. רב's case has no such person, so the fear of being caught is much weaker.
steps.whatToRemember: Being believed because 'it can be checked' only works well when someone is actually expected to check. A named claimant makes a liar afraid.

steps.title: רבי ירמיה בר אבא corrects the teaching: the ישראל is believed
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה בר אבא says רב יהודה got the teaching wrong through גידול. The real version is that a ישראל is believed to say he gave the בכור to a כהן already blemished.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה בר אבא said: Where did יהודה get this from? I taught it to גידול, and גידול taught it to him. But this is what I actually told him: a ישראל is believed to say, 'I gave this בכור to a כהן with its blemish.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה בר אבא steps in to fix how רב's teaching was passed down. He says the speaker who is believed is the ישראל, not the כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the version we were discussing, the כהן is believed about how he received the animal. רבי ירמיה בר אבא traces the chain (himself → גידול → רב יהודה) and says it changed along the way. In his original wording, the ישראל who gave the animal is the one believed. This makes sense because the ישראל gains nothing from saying it, since the בכור goes to the כהן anyway.

keyTerms.meaning: from where does he have (this)?
I set it / taught it to (him)
and this is what I told him
firstborn animal, given to a כהן
with its blemish (already present)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two versions. רב יהודה's version: the כהן is believed about what the ישראל gave him. רבי ירמיה בר אבא's version: the ישראל is believed about what he gave the כהן.
steps.whyThisMatters: Changing who is believed changes the reason for the rule. It is not only that the fact can be checked. The ישראל also has no personal interest in lying, which makes him more trustworthy than a כהן speaking for his own benefit.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya bar Abba said:
From where does Yehuda have this?
I taught it to Giddul,
and Giddul taught it to him (Yehuda).
phrases.notes: So the teaching was changed along the way.

phrases.english: But this is what I told him:
An Israelite is believed to say:
'I gave this firstborn to a priest with its blemish.'
phrases.notes: So the כהן may slaughter and eat it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה בַּר אַבָּא: מְנָא לֵיהּ לִיהוּדָה הָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the original teaching of רב that the previous steps were trying to support, and corrects its wording.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A ישראל is believed to say he gave the בכור to the כהן when it already had its blemish.

steps.title: Why would we need to be told a ישראל is believed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי ירמיה בר אבא's version: of course a ישראל is believed, since he gains nothing from lying.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ישראל is believed? That is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the version of רבי ירמיה בר אבא from Step 4. It asks why anyone needs to say that a ישראל is believed, when that seems obvious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ישראל already gave the בכור away, so he has nothing to gain by saying it had a מום. Since he has no reason to lie, a teaching that he is believed seems unnecessary. The גמרא wants to know what new point this version adds.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious. The גמרא's way of asking why a teaching is needed at all.
A non-כהן Jew, here the original owner who gave the בכור away.

phrases.english: An Israelite? It is obvious!
phrases.notes: The ישראל gets nothing out of the בכור, so of course he is believed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for the corrected version given in Step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי ירמיה בר אבא's statement that a ישראל is believed.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A witness with nothing to gain is obviously trusted, so the statement seems to add nothing.

steps.title: The animal was small and grew up
steps.stepSummary: The teaching is needed for a case where the animal was young when given and grew bigger. We might have thought the ישראל cannot recognize it anymore, so we are taught that he is still believed.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is needed for an animal that was small and then grew. You might have said he cannot really be sure it is the same animal. So the teaching tells us he is believed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. It explains which case makes this teaching necessary: an animal that grew up between the giving and the testimony.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is not about honesty but about mistakes. Once the animal grows, its appearance changes, so maybe the ישראל is confusing it with a different בכור that the כהן blemished on purpose. The teaching tells us we trust the ישראל to recognize the animal he gave.

keyTerms.meaning: It is only needed for... The usual opening for explaining which case a teaching is about.
It was small and grew up.
You might have said... It introduces the mistaken assumption.
He knows it clearly, he is sure.
It teaches us, meaning the new point being made.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the worry is that the ישראל is lying. He has no reason to lie. The worry is only that he made an honest mistake in identifying the animal.

phrases.english: No, it is needed for a case where it was small and grew,
lest you say: he is not certain of it (he doesn't recognize it),
phrases.notes: Its looks have changed, so maybe he is confusing it with another animal.

phrases.english: it teaches us otherwise.
phrases.notes: He is trusted to recognize it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא challenge of Step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the teaching to a specific case (אוקימתא).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the animal grew, the ישראל may not recognize it and could be mistaken.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ישראל is trusted to identify the animal he gave, even after it grew.

steps.title: סורא, פומבדיתא, and the final ruling
steps.stepSummary: סורא learned like the second version, where only a ישראל is believed. פומבדיתא learned like the first version, where even a כהן is believed. The הלכה follows even the first version.
steps.simpleTranslation: In סורא they taught it like the later version. In פומבדיתא they taught it like the first version. And the הלכה is like even the first version.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports which version each ישיבה followed, then gives the final הלכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the second version (רבי ירמיה בר אבא), only the ישראל's testimony helps. Under the first version (רב יהודה in the name of רב), even the כהן himself is believed. By ruling 'even like the first version,' the גמרא goes with the more lenient view: a כהן who says he received the animal already blemished is believed.

keyTerms.meaning: סורא, a great Babylonian ישיבה.
פומבדיתא, another great Babylonian ישיבה.
The first version / the later version of a teaching.
The practical הלכה, the final ruling.

steps.whatToRemember: Final הלכה: even a כהן is believed to say that a ישראל gave him the בכור already blemished, following the first version (רב).
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical bottom line of the whole סוגיא about trusting claims of a pre-existing מום.

phrases.english: In Sura they taught in accordance with the latter version,
phrases.notes: Only the ישראל is believed (רבי ירמיה בר אבא).

phrases.english: in Pumbedita in accordance with the first version,
phrases.notes: Even the כהן is believed (רב יהודה in the name of רב).

phrases.english: and the halakha is in accordance with even the first version.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After both versions have been explained, the גמרא decides between them.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה follows the lenient first version: even a כהן is believed.

steps.title: A כהן tries to trick רפרם
steps.stepSummary: רפרם gave an unblemished בכור to a כהן, who then blemished it himself. Later the כהן brought it to רפרם and claimed a ישראל gave it to him blemished. רפרם recognized the animal and caught him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רפרם in פומבדיתא had a בכור and gave it to a כהן with no מום. The כהן went and made a מום in it. One day רפרם's eyes were weak, and the כהן brought the animal to him and said: 'A ישראל gave me this בכור with its מום.' רפרם forced his eyes open, saw it, and recognized it. He said to him: 'Wasn't I the one who gave it to you?'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story in פומבדיתא, the place that followed the first version, where a כהן lied about how his בכור got its מום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כהן blemished the animal himself, which is forbidden, and then tried to get it permitted by claiming it came already blemished. He even brought it to the very person who had given it to him, hoping רפרם's weak eyes would keep him from noticing. The story shows that a כהן's claim can be false, which makes us wonder whether the lenient ruling should still stand.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא in פומבדיתא who served as an expert examiner of מומים.
A firstborn animal (בכור).
He put (made) a blemish in it on purpose.
He forced his eyes open.

phrases.english: Rafram in Pumbedita had a firstborn animal,
and he gave it to a priest without a blemish.
The priest went and put a blemish in it.
One day Rafram's eyes were weak,
and the priest brought it before him.
phrases.notes: He brought it to רפרם, the expert, to be permitted.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: בְּכוֹר זֶה נָתַן לִי יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּמוּמוֹ.
phrases.english: He said to him: An Israelite gave me this firstborn with its blemish.
Rafram forced his eyes open and saw it, and recognized it.
phrases.notes: Sefaria takes בשקריה as 'recognized it.' It can also be read as 'saw through his lie.'

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לָאו אֲנָא דִּיהֵיבְתֵּיהּ לָךְ?
phrases.english: He said to him: Was it not I who gave it to you?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A story connected to the ruling that a כהן is believed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An incident where a כהן falsely claimed he received the בכור already blemished.

steps.title: One cheater does not make all כהנים suspect
steps.stepSummary: Even after catching the כהן lying, רפרם did not stop trusting כהנים. He said this one was unusually brazen, and other כהנים are not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even so, רפרם was not worried about the matter. This one is brazen, but the rest of the world is not brazen.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the story by telling us what רפרם took from it. One lying כהן did not change the general rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This כהן lied straight to the face of the man who gave him the animal, which takes extreme nerve. Ordinary כהנים would not act like that. So the rule that a כהן is believed (Step 7) stays in place.

keyTerms.meaning: He was not concerned about the matter.
Brazen, shameless.
Everyone else.

steps.whatToRemember: One shameless person does not overturn a general חזקה of trust. The הלכה that a כהן is believed still stands.
steps.whyThisMatters: The story backs up the final ruling by showing that even a real case of lying did not lead the חכמים to suspect all כהנים.

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲפִילּוּ הָכִי לָא חַשׁ לַהּ לְמִילְּתָא,
phrases.english: And even so, he was not concerned about the matter,
saying: it is this one who is brazen,
everyone else is not brazen.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲפִילּוּ הָכִי לָא חַשׁ לַהּ לְמִילְּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the lesson from the רפרם story and keeps the ruling of Step 7.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: An unusual brazen liar does not undermine the general trust in כהנים claiming the מום was already there.

steps.title: רב אשי: a birth blemish raises no concern
steps.stepSummary: A שרוע was brought to רב אשי. He ruled that there is no concern either way, since the blemish was clearly there from birth.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain שרוע animal came before רב אשי. He said: What should we worry about? Whether a כהן brought it or a ישראל brought it, this is a בכור that was born with its blemish.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a new story. A בכור with a natural, uneven-body blemish is brought to רב אשי, and he says we need not worry about who brought it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier steps worried that a כהן might blemish the animal on purpose, as in רפרם's story. A שרוע's blemish is part of how the animal was born, so nobody could have caused it. That is why רב אשי says it makes no difference who brought it.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal with one body part (here, an eye) larger than its pair, which is a blemish
What should we be worried about with it?
Its blemish is with it, meaning it was born with it

phrases.english: A certain animal with one oversized limb (eye)
that came before Rav Ashi,
he said: what should we be concerned about with it?

phrases.aramaic: אִי כֹּהֵן הוּא, אִי יִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא —
phrases.english: whether it is a priest, whether it is an Israelite —
this is a firstborn whose blemish is with it (from birth).

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא שָׂרוּעַ דַּאֲתָא לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב אָשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the story of a כהן who caused a blemish himself, this new case has a blemish that clearly could not have been caused by a person.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A בכור with a natural birth blemish may be examined and permitted no matter who brings it.

steps.title: רבינא: רב יהודה requires a כהן present
steps.stepSummary: רבינא points out that if a ישראל brought it, רב יהודה's rule requires a כהן to be present.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to רב אשי: But maybe it is a ישראל who brought it! And רב יהודה said: We do not examine a ישראל's בכור unless a כהן is there with him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא challenges רב אשי. He says a ישראל's case is still a problem, because of a known rule from רב יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה's rule is not about faking a blemish. It is about what happens after the animal is permitted: a ישראל left alone might keep the meat instead of giving it to the כהן. רבינא argues that this worry applies even when the blemish is natural.

keyTerms.meaning: But perhaps
We do not examine (the blemish)
A כהן is present with him

steps.confusionAlert: רבינא is NOT saying the ישראל might have caused the blemish. His worry is that once the animal is permitted, the ישראל might keep the כהן's animal for himself.

phrases.english: Ravina said to Rav Ashi:
But perhaps it is an Israelite,
and Rav Yehuda said:
we do not examine the firstborn of an Israelite
unless a priest is with him!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבִינָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי וְדִלְמָא יִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב אשי's claim that a ישראל bringing the animal raises no concern.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's statement that it does not matter whether a כהן or a ישראל brought it
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב יהודה requires a כהן to be present for a ישראל's בכור, so a ישראל alone should not be helped.

steps.title: רב אשי: רב יהודה's case is different
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי explains that רב יהודה's rule covers a case where a ישראל might steal the כהן's property.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said to him: How can you compare? There, granted, a ישראל will not eat sacred meat outside the Temple, but he is suspected regarding the כהן's money.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי begins his answer by explaining the reason behind רב יהודה's rule. This sets up the contrast with our case in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ישראל fears the serious sin of eating קדשים outside, so he will bring the animal to be checked. But once the animal is permitted, we suspect he may take what belongs to the כהן. That is why רב יהודה requires a כהן to be present.

keyTerms.meaning: How can you compare? The cases are not alike
Sacred meat eaten outside its proper place, a severe sin
Suspected
The money or property belonging to the כהן

phrases.english: He said to him: How can these be compared?!

phrases.aramaic: הָתָם, נְהִי דְּקָדָשִׁים בְּחוּץ לָא אָכֵיל,
phrases.english: There, granted that he will not eat sacred meat outside,
he is suspected regarding the priest's property.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבינא by narrowing רב יהודה's rule.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב יהודה's rule applies to every בכור brought by a ישראל.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב יהודה's rule rests on the worry that a ישראל may steal from the כהן. That worry applies only where nothing shows the ישראל is especially careful.

steps.title: Someone who honors the Sage won't steal
steps.stepSummary: Here the blemish is obvious, so the ישראל only came out of respect for the חכם. Such a person would not commit theft.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here, since he knows this is an obvious blemish, why did he bring it before the רבנן? Out of respect for the חכם. If he does not ignore the חכם's honor, would he do something forbidden?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי finishes his answer by explaining why our case is different. Here, the very act of coming to the חכם proves the ישראל is careful.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שרוע's blemish is a מום מובהק, so the owner did not need a חכם to know it is permitted. He came anyway out of respect for the חכם. A person that careful about a חכם's honor would surely not steal from a כהן, so no כהן needs to be present.

keyTerms.meaning: Since, after all
A clear, obvious blemish
The honor of the Sage
A forbidden act (here, stealing from the כהן)

steps.whatToRemember: רב יהודה requires a כהן to be present when a ישראל's בכור is examined, to protect the כהן's property. That rule does not apply to an obvious blemish, because a ישראל who still came to the חכם out of respect shows he is careful and can be trusted.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a person's behavior can remove a suspicion: coming to the חכם when it was not needed proves the owner's honesty.

phrases.english: Here, since he knows
that this is a clear-cut blemish,
why did he bring it before the Sages?
Because of the honor of the Sage;
the honor of the Sage he does not neglect,
yet he would commit a transgression?!

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא מִכְּדֵי יָדַע דְּהַאי מוּם מוּבְהָק הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the contrast begun in step 12 by explaining our case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases based on behavior that shows honesty
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A ישראל bringing an obvious blemish is suspected of stealing like any ישראל.
steps.terutzMaskana: His coming to the חכם when it was not needed shows he is careful, so he is trusted and no כהן is needed.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב אשי's ruling stands: with an obvious birth blemish, it does not matter whether a כהן or a ישראל brought the animal.

steps.title: Everyone is believed about blemishes on a tithe animal
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that anyone, even the owner, is believed when he testifies that a מעשר בהמה animal has a blemish.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Everyone is believed about the blemishes of a tithe animal.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה starts. It says that anyone, even the owner, may testify that a מעשר animal has a blemish, and we believe him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier in the פרק we saw worry that an owner might lie about a בכור so he can eat it. With מעשר, the משנה says there is no such worry, and everyone is trusted. The גמרא will now explain why מעשר is different.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for מַתְנִיתִין, 'our משנה'. Marks the start of a משנה.
Everyone is believed
Blemishes of an animal tithe (מעשר בהמה)

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a contrast with בכור, where the owner, and sometimes even a כהן, is not automatically trusted.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
Everyone is believed about the blemishes of a tithe animal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה after the story of רב אשי and the שרוע.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Anyone, including the owner, is believed to say that a מעשר animal is blemished.

steps.title: Why is everyone believed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the משנה's rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why even the owner is trusted about a מעשר blemish. This question sets up the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The owner gains from the ruling, because a blemished מעשר animal may be eaten as חולין-style meat anywhere. Normally we might suspect him of lying. So the גמרא wants the logic that removes that suspicion.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for גְּמָרָא. Marks the start of the discussion on the משנה.
What is the reason?

phrases.english: GEMARA:
What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the משנה in step 14.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the owner, who gains from the ruling, is still believed about a מעשר blemish.

steps.title: He could have blemished it from the start
steps.stepSummary: First answer: the owner could have legally given the animal a blemish before it became holy, so he has no reason to lie.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because if he wanted, he could have put a blemish in it from the beginning!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the owner is trusted because he could have legally made a blemish in the animal before tithing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before tithing, the animal is not holy yet, so giving it a blemish is allowed. Since the owner could have gotten the same result honestly, we assume he would not bother lying. This is a kind of מיגו reasoning.

keyTerms.meaning: If he wanted
Throw (put) a blemish into it
From the beginning, before tithing

phrases.english: Because if he wanted,
he could have put a blemish in it from the beginning!

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאִי בָּעֵי שָׁדֵי בֵּיהּ מוּמָא מֵעִיקָּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The owner had a legal way to blemish the animal before it became מעשר, so he has no motive to lie.

steps.title: He cannot know which animal will be tenth
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: the owner cannot know ahead of time which animal will come out tenth, so how could he blemish that specific one?
steps.simpleTranslation: Who knows which one will come out?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer. The animals pass through a gate one by one, and nobody knows in advance which one will be tenth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in step 16 assumed the owner could target the specific animal that becomes מעשר. But that animal is only chosen when it happens to come out tenth. So he could not have blemished 'it' in advance.

keyTerms.meaning: Who knows?
Which one will go out (as the tenth)

phrases.english: Who knows which one will come out?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the owner could have blemished this specific animal from the start.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The tenth animal is decided only when it passes through the gate, so it cannot be identified and blemished beforehand.

steps.title: He may not arrange which animal comes out tenth
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא blocks a possible defense: the owner cannot set up a chosen animal to come out tenth, because the תורה says 'לא יבקר בין טוב לרע'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say he leads it out at the head of the ten, the Merciful One said: 'He shall not search between good and bad'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא imagines a fix: maybe the owner deliberately sends out a chosen animal as number ten. It rejects this fix with a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק 'לא יבקר בין טוב לרע' teaches that the owner may not choose which animal becomes מעשר. The animals must come out on their own. So the first answer still does not work.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say
At the 'head' of the ten, the one that ends the group as tenth
He shall not search between good and bad (ויקרא כז:לג)
The Merciful One (the תורה) said

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new question. The גמרא is closing off a possible escape route for the answer of step 16, so the challenge of step 17 still stands.

phrases.english: And if you would say
he leads it out as the head of the ten,
'He shall not search between good and bad,'
the Merciful One said!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא מַפֵּיק לֵיהּ בְּרֵישׁ עַשְׂרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects a possible defense of step 16 against the challenge in step 17.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggestion that the owner could deliberately send out a chosen animal as tenth.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The תורה forbids choosing which animal becomes מעשר (לא יבקר).

steps.title: He could have blemished his whole flock
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא revises the answer: the owner could have legally blemished every animal in the flock before tithing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, because if he wanted, he could have put a blemish in his entire flock.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the corrected reason. The owner did not need to know which animal would be tenth, because he could have blemished all of them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If every animal were blemished before tithing, whichever came out tenth would surely be blemished. Since that legal option existed, the owner has no reason to lie. The rule of the משנה is now explained.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (introduces a corrected explanation)
His entire flock

steps.whatToRemember: Everyone, even the owner, is believed about מעשר blemishes, because the owner could have legally blemished his whole flock before tithing. Lying would gain him nothing.

phrases.english: Rather, because if he wanted,
he could have put a blemish
in his entire flock.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא דְּאִי בָּעֵי שָׁדֵי בֵּיהּ מוּמָא בְּכוּלֵּיהּ עֶדְרֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fixes the answer of step 16 so it survives the challenges of steps 17 and 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the original answer (from one animal to the whole flock)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The owner could have blemished the specific animal that became מעשר.
steps.terutzMaskana: The owner could have blemished the entire flock, so no specific choosing was needed.

steps.title: A בכור with an obvious blemish may be permitted by three ordinary people
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: a בכור that is blind in one eye, has a cut-off foreleg, or a broken hind leg may be slaughtered based on three ordinary people.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A בכור whose eye was blinded, whose foreleg was cut off, or whose leg was broken may be slaughtered based on three members of the synagogue.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה starts. For a בכור with a very obvious, serious blemish, three ordinary people may permit it to be slaughtered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a בכור needs a מומחה to decide whether its blemish is permanent. Here the blemishes are so obvious that no expertise is needed. So the תנא קמא lets three regular people decide.

keyTerms.meaning: Firstborn male animal, which belongs to the כהן
Its eye was blinded
Its foreleg was cut off
Its hind leg was broken
Three ordinary people who attend the synagogue (not experts)

phrases.english: MISHNA:
A firstborn whose eye was blinded,
or whose foreleg was cut off,
or whose hind leg was broken —
this may be slaughtered
based on three members of the synagogue.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה about who may permit a בכור.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For an obvious permanent blemish, three ordinary people may permit a בכור to be slaughtered, without a מומחה.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: Only an expert may permit it
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי disagrees: even a court of twenty-three cannot permit the בכור; only a מומחה can.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: Even if there are twenty-three there, it may be slaughtered only based on an expert.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי argues with the first opinion in the משנה. He says even an obvious blemish needs a מומחה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוסי, the deciding factor is not how many people judge or how important they are, but whether one of them is an expert in blemishes. Even a full court of twenty-three without a מומחה is not enough. The two opinions argue about whether an obvious blemish removes the need for an expert.

keyTerms.meaning: Twenty-three, the size of a court that can judge capital cases
An expert in judging blemishes

steps.whatToRemember: The תנא קמא lets three ordinary people permit a בכור with an obvious blemish. רבי יוסי requires a מומחה no matter what, even instead of twenty-three judges.
steps.whyThisMatters: This argument is about whether the need for a מומחה is only practical, needed when the blemish is unclear, or a fixed requirement for permitting any בכור.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says:
Even if there are twenty-three there,
it may not be slaughtered
except based on an expert.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר אֲפִילּוּ יֵשׁ שָׁם עֶשְׂרִים וּשְׁלֹשָׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A disagreeing opinion within the same משנה as step 20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only a מומחה may permit a בכור to be slaughtered, even if the blemish is obvious and twenty-three judges are present.

steps.title: Three ordinary people can permit a firstborn outside the Land
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens with a teaching, reported with two versions of who said it in whose name: outside ארץ ישראל, a בכור may be permitted for slaughter by three ordinary people.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רבי שמלאי and רבי יהודה נשיאה both said in the name of רבי יהושע בן לוי. Some say it was רבי שמלאי and רבי יהושע בן לוי, both saying it in the name of רבי יהודה נשיאה: Permitting a בכור outside ארץ ישראל can be done by three ordinary members of the synagogue.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins discussing the משנה by quoting an אמורא's rule. Three regular Jews can permit a בכור outside ארץ ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The chain of names is reported in two versions ("ואמרי לה"), but the rule itself is the same in both. Outside ארץ ישראל, a בכור could never be brought as a קרבן anyway. So the rule eases who may judge its blemish: an expert is not needed, and three regular people are enough.

keyTerms.meaning: Abbreviation for גְּמָרָא; the discussion of the משנה begins here
Both of them
And some say (introduces a different version of the tradition)
Permitting a firstborn animal to be slaughtered and eaten because of a blemish
Outside ארץ ישראל
Regular synagogue-goers, meaning ordinary people who are not experts

steps.confusionAlert: The two versions only disagree about who quoted whom. The הלכה being taught is identical in both versions.

phrases.english: Gemara:
Rabbi Simlai and Rabbi Yehuda Nesia

phrases.aramaic: תַּרְוַיְיהוּ מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי אָמְרִי,
phrases.english: both say in the name of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ: רַבִּי שִׂמְלַאי וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
phrases.english: and some say: Rabbi Simlai and Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi

phrases.aramaic: תַּרְוַיְיהוּ מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יְהוּדָה נְשִׂיאָה אָמְרִי:
phrases.english: both say in the name of Rabbi Yehuda Nesia:
The permitting of a firstborn outside the Land
is by three members of the synagogue.
phrases.notes: These are ordinary people, not a מומחה.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׂמְלַאי וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה נְשִׂיאָה תַּרְוַיְיהוּ מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי אָמְרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the משנה of steps 20-21 with an אמורא's ruling about three ordinary people.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Outside ארץ ישראל, three ordinary people may permit a בכור for slaughter.

steps.title: רבא limits it to obvious blemishes
steps.stepSummary: רבא adds a limit: three ordinary people may permit the בכור only when the blemish is clear-cut and obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: And only with clear-cut blemishes.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא narrows the rule from step 22. Three regular people may decide only when the blemish is obvious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ordinary people cannot be trusted to judge borderline or subtle blemishes. For those, a מומחה is needed. Three people are enough only for blemishes that anyone can recognize.

keyTerms.meaning: A leading אמורא of Babylonia
Blemishes
Clear-cut, obvious

steps.whyThisMatters: This limit sets the scope of the leniency. It is the point the next two steps argue about.

phrases.english: Rava said:
And with clear-cut blemishes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a qualification to the ruling in step 22.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Three ordinary people may permit a בכור only when the blemish is clear-cut.

steps.title: Isn't רבא's point already in the משנה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבא adds. The משנה already lists clear-cut blemishes (a blinded eye, a cut-off foreleg, a broken hind leg) and allows three ordinary people for them.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is he teaching us? We already learned in the משנה: A בכור whose eye was blinded, whose foreleg was cut off, or whose hind leg was broken may be slaughtered based on three members of the synagogue!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא for saying something that seems to be in the משנה already. The משנה only gives obvious blemishes as its examples.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's three examples are all obvious blemishes. So it seems we already know that three people are enough for clear-cut blemishes. רבא's statement looks unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: What is he teaching us? (asks what a statement adds)
We already learned it (in a משנה)
Its eye was blinded
Its foreleg was cut off
Its hind leg was broken

phrases.english: What is he teaching us? We learned:
A firstborn whose eye was blinded,
or whose foreleg was cut off, or whose hind leg was broken —

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי זֶה יִשָּׁחֵט עַל פִּי שְׁלֹשָׁה בְּנֵי הַכְּנֶסֶת!
phrases.english: this may be slaughtered based on three members of the synagogue!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's statement in step 23 as already stated in the משנה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה's examples are all clear-cut blemishes, so רבא's limit seems to be already known.

steps.title: The משנה's examples might have been chosen to show רבי יוסי's strictness
steps.stepSummary: Without רבא, one might read the משנה's obvious examples as chosen only to show how strict רבי יוסי is, and think the Rabbis allow three people even for unclear blemishes. רבא teaches that this reading is wrong.
steps.simpleTranslation: If we only had the משנה, I would have said that outside ארץ ישראל three people may permit even blemishes that are not clear-cut. I would have thought the משנה lists clear-cut blemishes only to show how far רבי יוסי goes. So רבא teaches us that it is limited to clear-cut blemishes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question by showing that the משנה could have been read differently. רבא's statement rules out that other reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי says only a מומחה may permit, even for these obvious blemishes. One could think the משנה picked obvious cases just to make רבי יוסי's opinion sound as extreme as possible, and that the first opinion would allow three people for any blemish. רבא teaches that the first opinion also allows three people only for clear-cut blemishes.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
I would have said (a mistaken first assumption)
To show you the strength (how far an opinion goes)
That are not clear-cut

steps.confusionAlert: "להודיעך כחו דרבי יוסי" is part of the mistaken first assumption (the הוה אמינא). It is not the conclusion. The conclusion is that the limit to clear-cut blemishes is real.
steps.whatToRemember: Three ordinary people can permit a בכור only for clear-cut blemishes. רבא is needed so that we do not read the משנה's examples as chosen only to show רבי יוסי's strictness.

phrases.english: If from the Mishnah, I would have said:

phrases.aramaic: בְּחוּצָה לָאָרֶץ אֲפִילּוּ מוּמִין שֶׁאֵין מוּבְהָקִין,
phrases.english: outside the Land, even blemishes that are not clear-cut,
and the fact that it teaches clear-cut ones —
is to show you the strength of Rabbi Yosei's view,
phrases.notes: רבי יוסי requires a מומחה even for obvious blemishes.

phrases.english: so he teaches us (that it is not so).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 24 by showing the משנה alone was unclear.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The משנה could be read another way, and the אמורא removes that reading
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה listed obvious blemishes only to show רבי יוסי's strictness, so three people could permit even unclear blemishes.
steps.terutzMaskana: Three people may permit only for clear-cut blemishes.

steps.title: Three people may permit where no expert is available
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes רבי ירמיה בר אבא, though רב יהודה was unsure whether רבי ירמיה בר אבא said it in the name of רב or of שמואל: three people may permit a בכור where there is no מומחה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said that רבי ירמיה בר אבא said, unsure whether it was in the name of רב or in the name of שמואל: Three people may permit a בכור in a place where there is no expert.
steps.whatsHappening: A new rule is brought. In a place without an expert, three people may permit a בכור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a second ruling about three ordinary people. It frames the leniency in terms of the expert being absent. The source was uncertain between רב and שמואל, but the rule itself is not in doubt.

keyTerms.meaning: Unsure whether it was said in the name of
Permit
An expert in judging blemishes
In a place where there is not

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה בַּר אַבָּא,
phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rabbi Yirmeya bar Abba said,

phrases.aramaic: סָפֵק מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב, סָפֵק מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דִּשְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: perhaps in the name of Rav, perhaps in the name of Shmuel:
Three permit the firstborn
in a place where there is no expert.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה בַּר אַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new אמורא ruling on the same topic of three ordinary people.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Three people may permit a בכור where no מומחה is available.

steps.title: Isn't this rule also already in the משנה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רב יהודה's rule adds, since the משנה already says that three members of the synagogue may permit a בכור.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is he teaching us? We already learned: This may be slaughtered based on three members of the synagogue!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks the same kind of question again, this time about רב יהודה's rule. The answer comes in the next part of the גמרא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה already allows three ordinary people to permit a בכור. So רב יהודה's rule seems to repeat the משנה. The גמרא now has to show what this rule adds.

keyTerms.meaning: This one, it
May be slaughtered
Based on the word of

phrases.english: What is he teaching us? We learned:

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי זֶה יִשָּׁחֵט עַל פִּי שְׁלֹשָׁה בְּנֵי הַכְּנֶסֶת!
phrases.english: this may be slaughtered based on three members of the synagogue!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן? תְּנֵינָא: הֲרֵי זֶה יִשָּׁחֵט עַל פִּי שְׁלֹשָׁה בְּנֵי הַכְּנֶסֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 26 as already taught in the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's rule that three people may permit where there is no מומחה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה already says three members of the synagogue may permit a בכור, so the rule seems to add nothing.

steps.title: Three people work only when no expert is around
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רב יהודה adds a limit. From the משנה alone, one might think three ordinary people may permit a בכור even where a מומחה is present. רב יהודה teaches that they may do so only when no מומחה is available.
steps.simpleTranslation: If we only had the משנה, I would have said that three people may permit it even where there is an expert. So he teaches us: where there is no expert, yes; where there is an expert, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is answering the question from step 27 about what רב יהודה's rule adds beyond the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says three members of the synagogue may permit a בכור, but it does not say whether this applies even when an expert is present. רב יהודה's words 'where there is no מומחה' supply that limit. Three ordinary people are a fallback only. They are not an equal alternative to the expert.

keyTerms.meaning: I would have said (the mistaken first assumption)
he teaches us (the new point being added)
an expert in judging the blemishes of animals
yes / no

steps.whatToRemember: Three ordinary people may permit a בכור only when no מומחה is available. If an expert is present, the three may not rule.

steps.title: Three people may permit a firstborn or annul a vow
steps.stepSummary: רב חייא בר עמרם gives two parallel rules. Three ordinary people may permit a בכור where there is no מומחה. Three ordinary people may annul a נדר where there is no חכם.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חייא בר עמרם said: Three people may permit a firstborn animal where there is no expert. Three people may annul a vow where there is no Sage.
steps.whatsHappening: A new אמורא, רב חייא בר עמרם, states two parallel rules. In each, three ordinary people take the place of a missing expert.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first half matches what רב יהודה just said about the בכור. The second half adds a new area: annulling vows. Normally a single חכם can annul a vow, but without one, a group of three ordinary people can do it.

keyTerms.meaning: permit or release (here it covers both permitting a בכור and annulling a vow)
a vow
a Sage, a Torah scholar qualified to annul vows alone

steps.whyThisMatters: The first half looks like a repeat of רב יהודה's rule. That sets up the גמרא's next move, which explains each half of this statement in turn.

phrases.english: Rav Ḥiyya bar Amram said:

in a place where there is no expert,
three people may annul the vow
in a place where there is no Sage.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new אמורא whose first rule parallels רב יהודה's, and adds a second rule about vows.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Without a מומחה, three people may permit a בכור. Without a חכם, three people may annul a נדר.

steps.deeperAnalysis: This exact rule was just taught by רב יהודה in step 26. The גמרא quotes each half of רב חייא בר עמרם's statement in turn to explain it. The explanation of this half continues on the next amud.
